titleTag: US Visa Emergency Appointment: Criteria and Proof Needed
h1: US Visa Emergency Appointments: What Qualifies, What Does Not, and the Proof You Need
deck: It is free, it is decided by the consular section rather than by anything you pay, and the list of accepted reasons is much shorter than most applicants assume. Weddings and graduations are on the wrong side of it.
metaDescription: US visa emergency appointment criteria: which reasons qualify, which are explicitly refused, the documents each one needs, and the order the request has to be made in.
keywords: how to request expedited visa interview
coverAlt: US visa emergency appointment criteria: urgent medical care, the funeral of an immediate family member in the United States, and students within 60 days of a programme start date qualify, while weddings, graduations, conferences and last-minute tourism are explicitly refused

headline: Three reasons in.
Everything else out.
coverSpec.title: US visa expedited appointment requests: three categories qualify and the common ones are explicitly refused
coverSpec.desc: Consular sections may expedite an interview for an urgent unforeseen situation. In practice that means urgent medical care with a doctor's letter and a letter from the treating US hospital, the funeral or repatriation of an immediate family member in the United States, or a student or exchange visitor within 60 days of a programme start date with an original I-20 or DS-2019 and proof of the SEVIS fee. Weddings, graduations, assisting pregnant relatives, annual conferences and last-minute tourism are named as not qualifying.

faq.q: What qualifies as an emergency for a US visa appointment?
faq.a: Consular sections describe it as an urgent, unforeseen situation such as a funeral, a medical emergency, or a school start date. In practice three categories carry: urgent medical care in the United States, the funeral or repatriation of an immediate family member there, and students or exchange visitors within 60 days of a programme start date. Everything else is decided case by case and most of it is refused.

faq.q: What does not qualify for an expedited US visa appointment?
faq.a: Consular guidance names these explicitly: travel to attend weddings or graduation ceremonies, travel to assist a pregnant relative, attending an annual business, academic or professional conference, and last-minute tourism. They are ordinary reasons to want an earlier date and they are not urgent unforeseen situations, so submitting one tends to spend the credible request you had.

faq.q: What proof do I need for a medical emergency request?
faq.a: Two letters, not one. A letter from your doctor describing the medical condition and explaining why care is being sought in the United States, and a letter from the physician or hospital in the United States indicating that they are prepared to treat the case. A request with only the first of those is the most common reason a genuine medical emergency is refused.

faq.q: Who counts as an immediate family member for a funeral request?
faq.a: Consular guidance defines it narrowly: mother, father, brother, sister or child. The death has to be in the United States, and the purpose is attending the funeral or making arrangements to repatriate the body. Grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins and in-laws sit outside that definition however close the relationship actually is, which is a hard thing to be told and better learned before you apply than after.

faq.q: Can students get an expedited appointment?
faq.a: Yes, within a defined window. The option is limited to students and exchange students within 60 days of their programme start date, and it requires an original Form I-20 or Form DS-2019 showing that start date together with evidence that the SEVIS fee has been paid. Outside 60 days the route is not open, which is a strong argument for starting the process as early as your documents allow.

faq.q: Do I have to book a normal appointment before requesting an expedite?
faq.a: Yes, and this order catches people out constantly. You submit the DS-160, pay the application fee, and schedule the first available interview appointment. Only then will a consular section consider an expedite request. It is an upgrade to an existing booking, not a way to book from nothing, and you should keep the original appointment until a decision comes back.

faq.q: Is an emergency appointment the same as the $750 paid expedite?
faq.a: No, and they are easy to confuse. The emergency request is free, discretionary, available at posts worldwide and decided on documented urgency. The $750 expedited appointment is a paid pilot running only at designated missions, currently Mission Mexico and Mission Canada, for B-1 and B-2 applicants, and it is not assessed on urgency at all. If you qualify on urgency grounds, make the free request first.

cta.heading: If your reason is real, make the free request first
cta.body: We would rather say that plainly than sell you something you do not need. An expedite request on documented urgency costs nothing and it beats anything a paid service can offer, ours included. Where it does not apply, because your reason is genuine but not on the list, the mechanism that is left is rescheduling, and that is what we do. Tell us your post, your current date and your deadline, and we will tell you honestly which of the two you should be using.
